Subject: Redwood Private VPC — follow-up & requested next tests

Hi David,

Thanks again for the call this morning — good to meet the ACME team and hear more about the EHR latency targets and the compliance constraints you have for PHI. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned: 

- What we heard: you need a private deployment option that can run inside your VPC or air-gapped datacenter, strict control-plane isolation (no egress for metadata), KMS-backed keys, and predictable latency for 99th percentile inference under 200ms for clinical-read workloads.
- Competitive concerns you raised: how Redwood Private differs from hyperscaler-managed endpoints (AWS/GCP) and other inference APIs, especially around control plane telemetry and network egress.

Proposed next actions:
1) Technical POC: run a small-scale private deployment in your staging VPC to validate network flows and egress rules (we'll provide a network checklist).
2) Benchmarks: we'll run a focused throughput/latency test vs your sample prompts and share token-level breakdowns.
3) Security evidence: we will share our SOC2 artifacts and a short whitepaper on control-plane design for Private installs.

Can you confirm the staging VPC CIDR and whether the deployment will be behind a firewall that blocks all outbound except to your internal KMS (or will you allow one-way pull from a management endpoint)? Also, is the ACME security team OK with a week-long POC that includes a brief maintenance window for an initial agent install?

I'll loop in Aditya (solutions) and Marissa (private deployments) to scope the tests and timeline. Suggest we schedule the first POC kick-off next Wednesday (6/17) if that works.

Thanks,

Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales Lead
Redwood Inference

Hi Vanessa,

Appreciate the summary. A few clarifications from our side:

- Staging VPC: 10.18.0.0/16 (we can carve out a /24 for the POC).
- KMS: We run keys in a customer-managed HSM cluster that does not allow external network calls. Ideally the control plane does not require outbound connectivity to a Redwood-managed endpoint.
- Air-gap feasibility: our security team asked specifically whether "control plane offline" deployment is supported (i.e., air-gapped with only internal registry and local KMS). If you have a short doc on that, please send it.

We're also evaluating hyperscaler options (Vertex AI + private endpoints, and AWS PrivateLink) — main differences we're watching for: where the control plane runs, whether telemetry is sent off-prem, and how rollback/updates are managed for model changes.

6/17 works for the kick-off. Please include a brief test plan so our infra team can provision the /24 and a jumpbox.

Thanks,

David Jenkins
CTO, ACME Health

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>

Vanessa / Marissa — quick tech notes and proposed plan below. I can produce the one-pager and test scripts today.

1) Air-gapped / control-plane options:
   - Fully air-gapped: Yes — we support an on-prem Private deployment where the control plane components are deployed inside the customer's network. In this mode, no metadata/telemetry leaves the customer's environment. The customer needs to host the control plane services and an internal registry for images. Updates are handled via signed artifacts the customer pulls from an offline bundle (we provide the bundle and verification steps).
   - Hybrid: if customers prefer a managed control plane, we offer a VPC-peered control plane option that requires outbound connectivity to specific management endpoints (we can document exact FQDNs/IP ranges).

2) Network requirements (POC mode):
   - Outbound (only for hybrid managed control plane): HTTPS to management.redwood-inference.com (443) and optional S3 endpoints for artifact pulls. We provide a hardened cert pinning process.
   - Ports for data-plane / model inference are only internal (no public IP required).
   - HSM/KMS: if you run a customer HSM that blocks external calls, our deployment can be configured to call the local KMS endpoint.

3) Competitor comparisons (short bullets to share externally):
   - Hyperscalers (AWS/GCP): typically control plane is managed and telemetry/health checks often traverse provider networks; private endpoints reduce exposure but control plane still may be outside customer tenancy.
   - Other inference APIs: many require outbound telemetry or remote model stores. We differentiate by:
       * True private control plane option with air-gap bundles
       * Clear network checklist and token-level cost/latency visibility in our Console
       * Dedicated capacity option for predictable SLOs and canary rollback baked into the runtime

4) Proposed POC tests (what we'll run on 6/17):
   - Network connectivity validation (CIDR, firewall, KMS reachability, optional management endpoint)
   - Image pull and offline bundle install (for air-gapped option)
   - Latency/throughput run: 1k requests at production-like prompt distribution; record p50/p95/p99 and token-level breakdowns
   - Telemetry validation: ensure no egress for the fully air-gapped install; for hybrid, verify allowed endpoints only.

I'll attach a short network checklist and a sample k6 script for latency tests. Marissa — please confirm which engineer(s) from Private Deployments will join and whether we should plan a maintenance window.

Thanks,
Aditya
Staff Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

David — thanks for the quick replies and context. Per Aditya's note below, short answers and next steps: 

- Air-gap: Yes — we support a fully air-gapped Private deployment. For the POC we can run two variants: (A) hybrid managed control plane with narrow outbound rules (to demonstrate speed of provisioning and rollback), and (B) fully air-gapped customer-hosted control plane to validate zero egress.
- Network: I've attached the network checklist and an example install bundle flow. For the hybrid option the only outbound hosts are management.redwood-inference.com (443) and an optional artifact endpoint (we can provide IP ranges). For air-gapped installs, you only need an internal registry and local KMS/HSM access.
- Competitor diff: we'll send a short one-pager that compares Redwood vs AWS/GCP private endpoint models (control-plane location, telemetry, rolling updates, cost/latency predictability).

Next steps:
1) I will share the one-pager + k6 script and a short SOC2 evidence pack by EOD today (links above).
2) Please provision a /24 from 10.18.0.0/16 and a jumpbox with SSH access for our engineer.
3) Kick-off call 6/17 10:00 AM PT — proposed invite attached. Expect Aditya + Marissa from our side to run the tests.

If ACME security wants to run the air-gapped install only, we can schedule a separate install window for that week as well.

Best,
